You are reviewing a proposed change for Go-Checkout Page ticket AMSD-1919, which addresses email validation case-sensitivity in the checkout form. The email and confirmEmail fields must match, and the proposal makes this comparison case-insensitive. Verify the implementation integrates correctly with the existing CheckoutForm validation architecture and does not introduce unnecessary new dependencies.
__REVIEWER_PROFILE__
STORY:__STORY_ID__Users entering matching email addresses in different cases (e.g., "User@Example.com" vs "user@example.com") currently fail form validation, creating friction in the checkout flow. The story proposes fixing this by making email comparison case-insensitive while maintaining all other validation behavior.

CHANGE TYPE:__CHANGE_TYPE__The change modifies the email/confirmEmail validation rule in CheckoutForm.tsx (around line 306) to normalize both values to lowercase before comparison. A regression test is added to the test suite under src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/__tests__/ to prevent case-sensitivity regressions.

BEFORE:
__BEFORE__The validation logic in src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/CheckoutForm.tsx performs case-sensitive email comparison. The validate rule uses types defined in CheckoutFormProvider.tsx and types.ts. Users with matching emails in different cases fail validation and cannot proceed.

AFTER:
__AFTER__The validation rule normalizes both email and confirmEmail to lowercase before comparing them, accepting matching emails regardless of case. Related type definitions and field handling remain unchanged. A test case verifies case-insensitive matching works as expected.
